english: Bookends\Near Cherbourg, France\D+15 1230 June 21, 1944
Marshall: At ease, Sergeant.  Have a seat.\  You... You want some coffee son?  It's fresh.\  Well, as fresh as it gets around here.
korean: 마셜: 편히 있게, 병장. 앉게.\커피 한잔 하겠나? 갓 끓였네.\뭐, 여기선 이게 최선이지.

english: Hartsock: Yes, sir.  Haven't had a good cup o' coffee in\  three or four days now.
korean: 하트삭: 네, 대령님. 제대로 된 커피는\사흘이나 나흘 만입니다.

english: Hartsock: Smells great.  Thank you, sir.
Marshall: Name and rank?

korean: 하트삭: 조 하트삭 병장입니다.\다들 레드라고 부릅니다.

english: Hartsock: So how long is this gonna take?\  Sir.
Hartsock: I'd just like to get back to my men.
Marshall: Second?\  Hartsock: Sir?

Hartsock: Oh!  Yes, sir.  2nd took heavy losses in\  Carentan. I was with 3rd at the time.

english: Marshall: Under Sgt. Matthew Baker?
Hartsock: Sort of, yes sir.
Marshall: Which brings us to Hill 30.
Marshall: Sgt. Baker did a good job on that line.
korean: 마셜: 베이커 병장은 그 전선에서 잘했어.

english: Marshall: Must have been one hell of a fight.
Hartsock: Baker didn't save us.
korean: 하트삭: 우릴 구한 건 베이커가 아닙니다.

english: Marshall: Excuse me, Sergeant?
Hartsock: Sorry, sir.
Hartsock: What I mean is... I've been hearing a lot of\  talk around here that Baker saved us at Hill 30,
korean: 하트삭: 제 말은... 30고지에서 베이커가\우릴 구했다는 얘기를 많이 들었습니다.

english: Hartsock: bringing in the 2nd Armored Division and all.
Hartsock: That's not what happened.
Leggett: I need armor support now!!
Leggett: I mean right now!!!
Hartsock: Leggett saved us.  Just no one wants to talk\  about it.
korean: 하트삭: 우릴 구한 건 레게트입니다.\아무도 그 얘길 안 하려 하죠.

english: Marshall: Why is that, Sergeant?
Leggett: TAKE ME!!!
Hartsock: He somehow managed to reach HQ on the radio.\  They sent the tanks.
korean: 하트삭: 무전으로 어떻게든 본부에 닿았고,\그들이 전차를 보냈습니다.

english: Marshall: I can't confirm that.  I thought Pvt.\  Leggett's radio wasn't working.
korean: 마셜: 확인이 안 되는군. 레게트 일병의\무전기는 고장 난 줄 알았네.

english: Hartsock: Couldn't receive, sir, but he was transmitting.
korean: 하트삭: 수신은 못 했지만 송신은 됐습니다.

english: Marshall: And Sgt. Baker?
Hartsock: He loved being in the thick of it.  Every time\  I turned around in Normandy he'd been knocked out by\  artillery or a mortar or some damn thing.
korean: 하트삭: 그는 늘 한복판에 뛰어들었죠.\노르망디에선 돌아볼 때마다 포탄이나\박격포에 맞아 쓰러져 있었습니다.

english: Hartsock: Yeah, he earned his stripes.  But so did the\  rest of us.
korean: 하트삭: 네, 계급장을 얻을 만했죠.\하지만 우리 모두 그랬습니다.

english: Hartsock: And I do mean earned.
Marshall: Baker got quite a scar.\  Is yours from that battle too?
korean: 마셜: 베이커에게 큰 흉터가 있더군.\자네 것도 그 전투에서 생겼나?

english: Drunken Man: How dare you touch my wife!
Hartsock: Can we just talk about Hill 30, sir?
Bookends\Near Cherbourg, France\D+15 1300 June 21, 1944
Hartsock: Can I speak candidly, sir?
Marshall: Of course, Sergeant.
Hartsock: Well, me and Baker... way before either\  one of us made Sergeant, used to joke about how\  jumping in a squad of thirteen is bad luck.
korean: 하트삭: 저와 베이커가 병장이 되기 전,\13명이 한 분대로 뛰면 재수 없다고\농담하곤 했습니다.

english: Marshall: That's a bit juvenile,\  don't you think, Sergeant?
Hartsock: Well, we were all so young then, sir.\  We even went so far as to paint a 13 on\  the back of our helmets...
korean: 하트삭: 그땐 다들 어렸습니다.\헬멧 뒤에 13까지 그려 넣었죠...

english: Hartsock: Basically saying if fate wants\  us fate can have us.
Hartsock: Like we weren't afraid.
Hartsock: But we were.
Hartsock: Seeing Desola like that...
Hartsock: I was afraid, sir.
Hartsock: I guess you could say I changed\  my mind at that point.
korean: 하트삭: 그때 생각이\바뀌었다고 할 수 있죠.

english: Marshall: Changed your mind?
Hartsock: Yeah, I decided fate\  couldn't have me...
korean: 하트삭: 네. 운명에게\절 내주지 않기로 했죠...

english: Hartsock: Or anyone else.
Marshall: Was this around the time\  when you were promoted to Sergeant?
Hartsock: It was around the time I started\  to act like one.
Hartsock: There was one person who was going\  to get me home safely to my family.
korean: 하트삭: 가족에게 무사히 돌아가게 해 줄\사람은 단 한 명뿐이었습니다.

english: Hartsock: And it wasn't Baker.
Hartsock: It was me.
Marshall: Then why did you go to St.\  Sauveur to fight?
Hartsock: Because I wasn't going to let the\  same thing happen to Doyle.
korean: 하트삭: 도일에게 같은 일이\생기게 둘 수 없었으니까요.

english: Bookends\Near Cherbourg, France\D+15 1330 June 21, 1944
Hartsock: That was five days ago.
Hartsock: I remember on the way to St. Martin he was\  going on and on about himself.  Sort of like a Doyle\  history lesson.
korean: 하트삭: 생마르탱 가는 길에 도일은\자기 얘기를 끝도 없이 했죠.\도일 역사 수업 같았습니다.

english: Doyle: Well, my full name is Seamus Doyle.
Doyle: You see, Seamus was my father's name, which is\  odd because I never knew my father, so I guess I never\  understood why my mother would name me after him.
korean: 도일: 셰이머스는 아버지 이름입니다.\전 아버지를 몰랐는데, 어머니가 왜\그 이름을 줬는진 모르겠습니다.

english: Doyle: And my mother, she was a piece of work. She once\  made me wash the dishes at three o' clock in the morning.
korean: 도일: 어머니도 대단했죠. 새벽 세 시에\절 깨워 설거지를 시킨 적도 있습니다.

english: Doyle: I mean she could cook like nobody's business,\  but the smell-
Doyle: She once caught my sister kissing this guy...\  stapled her dress shut.
korean: 도일: 누나가 남자와 키스하는 걸 보고...\드레스를 스테이플러로 박아 버렸죠.

english: Hartsock: That boy could talk.
Marshall: I think that's all the questions I have.
korean: 마셜: 질문은 이 정도면 된 것 같네.

english: Marshall: Everything you said is important,\  a lot of good we can learn from this.
korean: 마셜: 자네가 한 말은 모두 중요하네.\여기서 배울 게 많을 거야.

english: Marshall: Sergeant Hartsock, you should get some rest.
Hartsock: Still got miles to go before we rest, sir.
Corrion: That took a while.
Hartsock: Got a lot on my mind, Sam.
Marshall: Name and rank?
Corrion: Cpl. Sam Corrion, sir.
Baker: How did it go with Col. Marshall?
Hartsock: Oh you know, I talked his ear off.
Baker: Yeah me too.
Baker: You know, we should write a book.\  Baker and Red, Through Hell and Highwater.
korean: 베이커: 우리 책 하나 써야겠군.\베이커와 레드, 지옥과 격랑을 넘어.

english: Hartsock: Why not Red and Baker?
Baker: Because I made Sergeant before you did.
Hartsock: Fair enough.
Hartsock: If we ever get back to England,\  I'm buying you a whiskey.
korean: 하트삭: 영국에 돌아가면,\내가 위스키 한잔 살게.

english: Baker: I like whiskey.
Risner: I'm gonna have to shove through it.
Risner: Matt get the Hell out of here!
Risner: Dammit! I'm out of ammo!
Leggett: They are... dead. There were too many of em...\  God.
Leggett: I understand the large hearts of heroes,\  the courage of present times...
korean: 레게트: 영웅들의 큰 마음과,\이 시대의 용기를 이해한다...

english: Leggett: It's from a poem my dad used to read to\  me as a kid.
korean: 레게트: 어릴 때 아버지가 읽어 주던\시의 한 구절이야.

english: Leggett: It amazes me that something so beautiful could\  be a part of something so ugly.
korean: 레게트: 이렇게 아름다운 것이\이토록 끔찍한 것의 일부라니 놀라워.

english: Victory in Carentan\D+8 0930 June 14, 1944\Carentan, France
Hartsock: Why in the hell did you bring back that\  busted piece of crap?
korean: 하트삭: 대체 왜 그 망가진 고물을\도로 가져온 거야?

english: Corrion: Not sure, seemed like the right thing to do.
korean: 코리온: 몰라, 그래야 할 것 같았어.

english: Hartsock: What are you gonna do, bury it?\  Corrion: I might.
Mac: Knock off the chatter and fall in.
Mac: I'm not one for speeches so I'll make this short.
korean: 맥: 연설은 체질이 아니니 짧게 한다.

english: Mac: First, there's a Colonel Marshall here to interview\  some of you for General Eisenhower.
korean: 맥: 먼저, 아이젠하워 장군 때문에\마셜 대령이 몇 명을 면담할 거다.

english: Mac: Don't screw that up.
Mac: Second, I've been in the Army a long time and in some\  pretty good units...
korean: 맥: 둘째, 난 군 생활도 오래 했고\좋은 부대도 많이 겪었다...

english: Mac: but in all that time...
Mac: well, I just want to say that you guys did good.
korean: 맥: 그냥, 너희가 정말 잘했다고 말하고 싶다.

english: Mac: We lost some good men.
Mac: But at the same time, we sent a message to Hitler and\  his boys that we're coming for him - that his days\  are numbered.
korean: 맥: 하지만 히틀러와 그놈들에게도\우리가 간다는 걸 알렸다.\놈의 날도 얼마 안 남았다.

english: Mac: Now I've got a promotion to make.
Mac: Sergeant Hartsock - front and center!
Mac: Second squad needs a new leader and the\  responsibility is now yours.  Sew on these stripes or\  I'll cite you for being out of uniform.
korean: 맥: 2분대에 새 지휘관이 필요하다.\이제 네 책임이다. 계급장을 달아라.\안 달면 복장 불량으로 처벌한다.

english: Mac: All right, men... Second and third squad, fall out!
Mac: Sergeant Baker!
Mac: You know this isn't over right?  Hell of a thing\  we've been through these last eight days.  Welcome to\  the end of the beginning...
korean: 맥: 아직 끝난 게 아닌 거 알지?\지난 8일은 정말 지독했다.\이제 시작의 끝에 온 걸 환영한다...

english: Mac: Grab your gear troopers!
Mac: We've still got a war to fight!
Baker: Third Squad! You heard the man.\  Move out!
